entities.summary: The Paris Peace Agreements, officially the Comprehensive Cambodian Peace Agreements, was signed on 23 October 1991 and marked the official end of the Cambodian–Vietnamese War and the Third Indochina War. The agreement led to the deployment of the first UN peacekeeping mission since the Cold War and the first occasion in which the United Nations took over as the government of a state. The agreement was signed by nineteen countries.
